learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge of applied thermodynamics and heat transmission. Basic principles and their application to solving engineering problems.
Knows a wide range of energy production and distribution systems, and their applications in the energy industry or as an auxiliary part of other industries.

Identifies the relationships between the knowledge and skills on various industrial technologies acquired in previous subjects and their application in the specific domain of the thermal prime mover industry.
Applies techniques and methods from various disciplines for the analysis and design of combustion engines. Knows and understands the operation of combustion engines for vehicles.
Knows the different electronic and control systems used in engines and understands their operation.

In accordance with the professional competencies of this degree, the future graduate must be able to state the needs for the application of combustion engines, as well as undertake design and optimization projects for these machines.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, abilities, and skills in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Comparison of engines and current trends in design and application.
Definition of fundamental and comparison parameters.
Combustion processes. Characteristics and influencing factors.
Mechanical and thermal losses. Cooling and lubrication.

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of activities developed during the course, laboratory practices
Questionnaire on the content of practices and assignments

assessment_rules: The evaluation can follow a mixed system or a simple global final test. In the mixed system, course activities (including lab practices) account for 30% of the final grade, requiring a minimum of 4 out of 10, and their grade is conserved until the second call. The final written exam constitutes 70% of the final grade, requiring a minimum of 5 out of 10. Failure to achieve the minimum in the written exam results in failing the subject. The simple system consists of a global final test: a written exam (70%, min 5/10) and a questionnaire on practices and assignments (30%, min 4/10).
